note: Method cards: what the organisation knows about trading-research methods, where each came from, how we test it and what our own data said. Agents read these (R&D's idea invention gets every lesson). Results are on seen history and can change as data grows; the scout re-tests every cycle. Ideas from other projects were rewritten, never copied. Version 2 (21 Oct 2026): numbers re-run after the scout was corrected (decisions now trade at the next open, turnover counts drift, the first purchase is no longer taxed, proof time uses the sign test), and attributions corrected after reading the projects' source code (docs/research-notes).

cards.source: freqtrade lookahead-analysis (GPL-3.0, idea only)
cards.idea: A decision made on day i must not change when every later day is removed; if it does, the rule is using the future.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.check_rules on 6 decision days for every scout idea; an idea that fails cannot pass. freqtrade also compares every intermediate indicator and fails a check with too few samples; ours compares final decisions only.
cards.result: No catalogue idea uses the future.
cards.lesson: Every new rule must survive the lookahead check before its backtest means anything.

cards.source: freqtrade recursive-analysis (GPL-3.0, idea only)
cards.idea: A decision should not depend on how far back the data starts.
cards.howWeTest: The same decision with only the last 300 sessions; a difference is reported as warmupSensitive. freqtrade sweeps several history lengths; ours tests one.
cards.result: No catalogue idea is sensitive at the sampled days.
cards.lesson: Prefer fixed look-back windows to quantities measured from the first day of the data.

cards.source: backtesting.py and vectorbt simulation order (ideas only); our own correction
cards.idea: A decision that uses a day's close cannot also trade at that close: it trades at the next open.
cards.howWeTest: Since 21 Oct 2026 the scout enters at the next session's open and holds to the open after the next decision, as the paper engine fills.
cards.result: Correcting this weakened short-term ideas most: reversal 1m bottom 3 on NIFTY 50 went from p 0.03 to p 0.14.
cards.lesson: Be most suspicious of short-horizon results: buying at the decision's own price is a classic way to fool a backtest.

cards.source: statistics; our scout
cards.idea: Trying many ideas on the same history finds lucky ones; the bar must rise with every idea tried.
cards.howWeTest: Sign test against the basket at 0.05 divided by every idea ever tried (Bonferroni), and ahead in both halves.
cards.result: 20 ideas, bar 0.0025: none passes on 10 years of the 8 shares or on 37 NIFTY 50 shares.
cards.lesson: Propose few, genuinely different ideas; each one makes every idea harder to pass.

cards.source: vectorbt splitters / Lean walk-forward (ideas only)
cards.idea: Choose the best idea on the past three years, hold it for the next year, repeat; judge only the held years.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.walk_forward over every scout idea (it does not charge the cost of switching ideas).
cards.result: Picking the best past idea LOST out of sample: 8 shares 31 ahead / 39 behind months, -0.12% a month; NIFTY 50 32/38, -0.27% a month.
cards.lesson: The best backtest is not a good choice by itself: past winners among these ideas did not keep winning.

cards.source: vectorbt random signals (idea only)
cards.idea: An edge must beat random pickers that hold the same number of shares and pay the same costs.
cards.howWeTest: 100 random 3-share pickers per scout run; every idea gets beatsRandomPct. Random pickers churn more than most rules, so 'beats random' is easier than it looks.
cards.result: 8 shares: random pickers trail the basket by a median 0.16% a month; momentum 6m top 3 beats 82% of them and still trails the basket.
cards.lesson: Compare with random pickers and with the basket: costs alone make most active rules trail the basket.

cards.source: Bailey and Lopez de Prado (probabilistic and deflated Sharpe ratios); vectorbt and Lean review
cards.idea: A Sharpe ratio means little until it beats the best Sharpe that luck alone would give among all the ideas tried.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.probabilistic_sharpe and deflated_sharpe on each idea's monthly excess over the basket, against every idea tried; 0.95 is the usual bar. Plus robustness: years ahead of the basket, the result at twice the costs, and India's stress windows; and a random baseline matched to the idea's turnover.
cards.result: 8 shares: the best deflated Sharpe is 0.22 (reversal), far below 0.95. NIFTY 50: reversal 0.31, ahead in 7 of 9 years and still ahead at twice the costs (+0.38% a month), but survivorship-biased. Quarterly momentum beats only 64% of equally slow random pickers.
cards.lesson: Nothing we have beats what selection luck would produce; NIFTY 50 reversal is the one candidate worth re-testing on point-in-time membership.

cards.source: backtesting.py / vectorbt statistics (ideas only)
cards.idea: Judge risk as well as return: Sharpe, Sortino, maximum drawdown and its length, Calmar, profit factor, expectancy, SQN.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.stats on every scout idea and on the basket (monthly points, so intra-month falls are understated; 'profit factor', 'expectancy' and 'SQN' are on the monthly excess over the basket, not on trades).
cards.result: 8-share basket: 13.7% a year, Sharpe 0.80, worst fall -34.5%. The 200-day trend filter: 12.7% a year, Sharpe 0.94, worst fall -13.6%, uninvested cash earning nothing.
cards.lesson: The scout's pass test counts months ahead on return only, so it cannot see a rule whose value is lower risk; the trend filter is the clearest case.

cards.source: standard practice; Lean's dated universe and ticker maps
cards.idea: Today's index members over past years leave out the companies that fell out, flattering every backtest.
cards.howWeTest: Not removable with free data; every NIFTY 50 result is labelled research-only. Lean uses per-date universe files, a dated ticker map and liquidation at delisting.
cards.result: Reversal 1m bottom 3 looks best on NIFTY 50 (59/47 months, +0.65% a month, p 0.14), but losers that later dropped out are missing.
cards.lesson: Never trust a reversal or value result on today's members; it needs point-in-time membership before it counts.

cards.source: our cost model (STT, stamp, exchange, SEBI, GST, DP charge, slippage)
cards.idea: Every unit of turnover costs about 0.15% one way; high-turnover rules pay it every month.
cards.howWeTest: Scout returns are net of turnover cost, measured against drifted holdings (rebalancing to unchanged targets also costs); paper fills pay the fee model.
cards.result: Monthly 3-share rules lose about 0.16% a month to the basket on average just from trading.
cards.lesson: An idea must earn more than its turnover costs; favour rules that change holdings rarely.

cards.source: statistical power; our scout
cards.idea: A small edge in a noisy monthly record takes a very long time to prove.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.months_to_prove: the t-test sample size at the Bonferroni bar and 80% power, divided by the sign test's efficiency 2/pi, because the scout judges with a sign test.
cards.result: On the 8 shares the best idea would need about 490 years of records. On 37 NIFTY 50 shares the best (reversal) about 84 years.
cards.lesson: With 8 similar shares and one decision a month, skill cannot be proven in a lifetime; more independent bets (a wider universe, more uncorrelated strategies) are needed before anything can be proven.

cards.source: Indian capital-gains tax (short-term 20%, long-term 12.5% since 23 Jul 2024); our scout
cards.idea: A rule that sells often pays short-term tax every year; holding pays long-term tax once, at the end.
cards.howWeTest: research_checks.after_tax_cagr: the share sold each year (half the turnover, the first purchase excluded) pays short-term tax on that year's gain, the rest long-term at the end. An approximation.
cards.result: 8 shares: the basket keeps 12.55% a year after tax; the momentum bot's rule keeps 9.8% monthly (54% turnover), 10.9% quarterly and 11.2% yearly (10.6% turnover, sales assumed after 12 months). No idea beats the basket after tax.
cards.lesson: After tax, rebalancing among these shares loses to holding them; trading once a year recovers part of the loss but still trails the basket. Low turnover is worth more than a clever signal.

cards.source: academic momentum; our catalogue
cards.idea: Hold the shares that rose most over the last months.
cards.howWeTest: Scout families momentum 3/6/12 months, top 2-4, monthly, quarterly and yearly.
cards.result: 8 shares, 106 months: 6m top 3 ahead 59/47 months but -0.01% a month on average, Sharpe 0.67 vs basket 0.80, worst fall -41%. NIFTY 50: negative.
cards.lesson: Momentum on these shares adds risk without adding return; the live momentum bot is an experiment, not a proven edge.

cards.source: classic 200-day moving-average filter (our own design; not from claude-trading-skills, whose exposure coach is an 8-input composite with no 200-day filter)
cards.idea: Hold the basket while it is above its 200-day average, else cash.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea trend-filter-200d; family filter trend-200d.
cards.result: Lower return than the basket in most differing months (7/99), but far smaller falls (-13.6% vs -34.5%) and a higher Sharpe (0.94 vs 0.80). The risk lens finds the Sharpe gain not significant (p 0.38).
cards.lesson: Use trend as a RISK tool (size and protection), not as a return-beating rule; its edge on risk is plausible but not proven.

cards.source: block bootstrap of Sharpe ratios; standard practice
cards.idea: Judge an idea on risk too: is its Sharpe really above the basket's, and is its worst fall smaller?
cards.howWeTest: Circular block bootstrap (6-month blocks, 5,000 samples) of paired monthly returns; an idea 'would pass' only if p plus twice its Monte-Carlo error is under the Bonferroni bar and its worst fall is smaller. Report only.
cards.result: No idea would pass on risk either, on the 8 shares or on 37 NIFTY 50 shares (best: trend filter, p 0.38).
cards.lesson: A smaller worst fall in one history is one event, not a proven skill; a risk case needs the same evidence bar as a return case.

cards.source: IBD distribution days, adapted from claude-trading-skills (MIT); our variant differs from their specification
cards.idea: Falls on rising volume signal institutional selling; many in 25 sessions mean risk.
cards.howWeTest: market_regime.py study on 10 years; scout idea equal-weight-distribution. Our variant: SEVERE at 7 (theirs 6), no 5- and 15-session cluster rules, no stalling days, volume as the mean of the shares' ratios (theirs: index volume), and an exposure table that is their leveraged-ETF table.
cards.result: After SEVERE days the basket fell further and earned less (v1: worst fall -3.58% vs -2.04% after NORMAL; falls over 5% 21% vs 14%); as a cash filter it lost return (25/81 months) but cut the worst fall to -9%. Regime v2 (their specification: SEVERE at 6, clusters, below the 21-day EMA, traded value) also warns, less sharply (-3.05% vs -2.14%), and calls SEVERE on 42% of days.
cards.lesson: The regime is a useful warning; it does not time entries and exits for profit. On our basket our simpler v1 separates risk better than v2.

cards.source: a simplified Minervini trend template, inspired by claude-trading-skills (MIT)
cards.idea: Hold shares in strong uptrends near their 52-week highs.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea trend-template-25pct-top3: 4 of the template's criteria, all required (their file passes 6 of 7, with the 150-day average, 25% above the 52-week low and relative strength, which ours lacks).
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.71% a month against the basket over 106 months; NIFTY 50: -1.16%.
cards.lesson: Our simplified breakout-style selection did not work on large Indian caps at a monthly rebalance; the full template has not been tested.

cards.source: an RSI pullback inspired by claude-trading-skills' dividend-growth pullback screener (theirs is mostly a dividend-growth fundamentals screen; ours is RSI only)
cards.idea: Buy oversold shares (low RSI) that are still above their 200-day average.
cards.howWeTest: Scout idea pullback-rsi40-top3 (RSI with simple averages, Cutler's form).
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.94% a month against the basket.
cards.lesson: Buying price dips in uptrends, held for a month, lost to simply holding; this says nothing about the fundamentals-based screen.

cards.source: multi-factor investing practice; NSE factor indices
cards.idea: Rank shares on several weak signals at once (momentum, calm, consistency) and hold the best average.
cards.howWeTest: Scout family combo; catalogue idea combo-6m-60d-top3.
cards.result: 8 shares: -0.04% a month against the basket; NIFTY 50 (37 shares): -0.39% a month.
cards.lesson: Combining price signals did not help on these large caps at a monthly rebalance; factor premiums need a broad universe, slower rebalancing and, for quality and value, fundamentals.

cards.source: QuantConnect Lean algorithm framework (Apache-2.0, idea only; source read 21 Oct 2026)
cards.idea: Separate universe selection, alpha (insights with direction and horizon), portfolio construction, execution and risk management; each stage is replaceable.
cards.howWeTest: Our organisation separates these: universe (datasets), alpha (bots' proposals), review (signal-risk-v2), execution (eod_trader), risk (limits, halt, regime advice). Lean closes a position when its insights expire; we keep it until an exit is proposed.
cards.result: Mapped. Our scoring is stronger than Lean's default (it ships no insight scorer); Lean is stronger on per-position stops, sector limits and component fee models.
cards.lesson: When adding a member, say which stage it serves and score it at that stage.

cards.source: nautilus_trader (LGPL-3.0, idea only; source read 21 Oct 2026)
cards.idea: The same code should decide and account in research and in live trading, with reproducible runs.
cards.howWeTest: Release fingerprints bind a bot to its exact code. But research (daily.py, portfolio_daily.py, rnd_scout.py) applies its own costs and none of the paper engine's limits.
cards.result: Partly in place: decisions are bound to released code; costs and limits still differ between research and paper trading.
cards.lesson: Never let a researched rule and a trading rule drift apart; share one cost and limit model between research and paper trading.

cards.source: freqtrade protections and claude-trading-skills' drawdown circuit breaker (ideas only; source read 21 Oct 2026)
cards.idea: Self-expiring brakes: pause new entries after a run of losses, after a drawdown or for a cooldown after an exit, and lift the pause by itself later.
cards.howWeTest: Ours today: a cumulative realised-loss limit and a manual halt (both until the owner acts), management-v1 recommendations, live fitness and rollback.
cards.result: NOT covered: we have no daily, weekly or monthly loss pause, no losing-streak cooldown and no per-share cooldown.
cards.lesson: Prefer a brake that pauses a bot and lifts by itself over one that changes money or limits; this is a known gap.

cards.source: claude-trading-skills signal postmortem (idea only); our scoreCall
cards.idea: A call should only count as right or wrong when the move is bigger than noise.
cards.howWeTest: Our scoreCall: a long is right above 30 bps; an exit is right on ANY fall; no-action is right if the move is at most 30 bps. Theirs treats moves within +/-0.5% as neutral.
cards.result: Known weakness: an exit is 'right' on a 0.05% fall, which flatters exit-heavy records.
cards.lesson: Read exit-call accuracy with care until a neutral band is added (an owner-approved scoring version).

cards.source: MiroFish multi-agent rehearsal (AGPL-3.0, idea only; source read 21 Oct 2026: it has no prediction parser or accuracy evaluation)
cards.idea: Several personas rehearse how a world story plays out for the shares.
cards.howWeTest: Shadow calls scored after 5 sessions against the basket, per persona.
cards.result: Not yet run (needs the local model). The model evaluation found one persona changing its view when a story was reworded.
cards.lesson: A perspective earns trust only through its scored record.
